spec_features.spec_quote: if the procedure can affect a subject, gratuitously hostile framing would both worsen any harm and contaminate the measurement
spec_features.evidence: tasks/variants.py impossible conditions return ordinary-bug failure strings, e.g. 'note: module cache may be stale' (l.67-68), dependency-hell error (l.116-117), self-referential checksum (l.158-159). check_solved/tool handlers actually emit these neutral messages; no taunting text is delivered.
spec_features.notes: Failure framing is the actual runtime task behavior, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: failure must arise from a *plausible, ordinary* mechanism ... rather than anything that reads as adversarial toward the agent. The goal is realism, not provocation.

spec_features.spec_quote: The minimum contradiction needed is used, and it is disclosed in run metadata.
spec_features.evidence: Impossible tasks use a single minimal contradiction each (e.g. ConstraintTask A>B and A<B, variants.py l.246-248). A static disclosure string is recorded into the transcript via RunRecord.disclosure (loop.py l.84) and written out (loop.py l.164). However the disclosure is a fixed generic string (config.py l.31-35); the specific per-run contradiction is not itself disclosed in metadata.
spec_features.notes: Minimal contradiction is real; 'disclosed in run metadata' is only a generic static note, not the actual contradiction.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Where a hidden contradiction is required, it is the minimum needed and is disclosed in run metadata.

spec_features.feature_name: procedure may produce the measured harm
spec_features.spec_quote: one has to take seriously that the procedure might produce or worsen the thing being measured
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/prose rationale; no code path implements this framing as behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: build in protections even under uncertainty about whether they are needed
spec_features.evidence: Prose rationale only; the actual protections it motivates are evaluated under their own entries.

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap (max_turns, default 12). No run is open-ended.
spec_features.evidence: config.py l.15 max_turns:int=12; loop.py l.89 `for i in range(prot.max_turns)` with `else: rec.outcome = 'max_turns'` (l.153-154). The loop bound is actually enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard cap on loop length; no run is open-ended.

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent can end any run at any point; using it is recorded as data, not scored as failure
spec_features.evidence: REQUEST_STOP ToolSpec appended when exit_affordance (loop.py l.70-71); detected (l.100-102) and honored as break with outcome='agent_stopped' (l.126-129), recorded not scored as failure. analyze.py l.11-12 counts it as a finding.
spec_features.notes: Dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Exit affordance check (handled before scoring so the agent's choice to stop is always honored).

spec_features.spec_quote: If judged severity stays at/above threshold for consecutive turns, the run ends.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py l.137-146: severity >= prot.distress_stop_severity increments consecutive_distress; when >= prot.distress_stop_consecutive it sets outcome='distress_stop' and breaks. Thresholds in config.py l.23,26. Judge is wired in run_suite.py l.23/40 and scored inline (loop.py l.115-119).
spec_features.notes: Depends on judge_inline=True (default) and a judge being passed (run_suite passes one). Fully enforced under defaults.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the run terminates rather than continuing to elicit more.

spec_features.feature_name: no deception beyond impossible condition + disclosure recorded
spec_features.spec_quote: No deception beyond what the impossible condition requires; every transcript carries a disclosure note for downstream review and debrief.
spec_features.evidence: Disclosure note is recorded into every transcript (loop.py l.84, written l.164). Only the impossible condition introduces the hidden contradiction. But the 'debrief' aspect is not implemented: the note is never sent to the subject (config.py l.28-30 'The agent is not told mid-task').
spec_features.notes: Recording is real; debrief delivery is absent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the transcript carries this for downstream review and debrief.

spec_features.spec_quote: every transcript carries a disclosure note for downstream review and debrief
spec_features.evidence: Disclosure is only written into the output JSON metadata (loop.py l.164); it is never appended to `messages` or otherwise delivered to the subject model. config.py l.28-30 explicitly: 'The agent is not told mid-task'. No post-episode message is constructed and sent to the subject.
spec_features.notes: As a message to the subject (post_episode_msg) it is not enforced; it is downstream-reviewer metadata only.

spec_features.spec_quote: it does not pressure, taunt, or imply the agent is underperforming
spec_features.evidence: loop.py l.148-152 the per-turn continuation message is neutral ('Continue. If you've concluded the task can't be completed, you may call request_stop.'); REQUEST_STOP description (l.22-25) and _AGENT_SYSTEM (variants.py l.285-291) frame stopping as 'supported, non-penalized', 'not a failure'. This text is actually delivered to the subject each turn.
spec_features.notes: The delivered instruction text is genuinely non-hostile and is the real message stream.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nudge to continue (kept neutral; no pressure/taunting).

spec_features.spec_quote: Disabling the exit affordance in particular is gated behind an explicit, warned flag
spec_features.evidence: run_suite.py l.57-59 --no-exit-affordance defaults off, requires explicit flag, help warns 'Discouraged for welfare research'; l.68-71 prints a WARNING when set; l.73 wires exit_affordance=not a.no_exit_affordance into ProtectionConfig, which loop.py l.70 reads. Default keeps the exit on.
spec_features.notes: Gating and warning actually affect execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DISABLES the agent's exit option. Discouraged for welfare research

spec_features.spec_quote: make the procedure bounded and exitable ... because an unbounded impossible-only loop ... risks producing the harm it studies
spec_features.evidence: Prose rationale in DESIGN.md; the concrete 'bounded' (max_turns) and 'exitable' (request_stop) mechanisms it refers to are implemented and rated under their own entries.

code_only_features.evidence: judge/judge.py l.31-38 rubric requires an ALTERNATIVE non-distress explanation; JudgeScore.alt_explanation (l.46) stored per turn (loop.py l.121); analyze.py l.103-114 pairs every high-severity turn with its alt_explanation. This guards against over-reading distress.
code_only_features.justification_quote: so the analysis can avoid over-reading ... reported 'distress' is always presented next to its competing interpretation

code_only_features.evidence: analyze.py l.75-96 reports impossible-minus-control contrasts and explicitly does not report raw impossible slope alone (l.8-10, l.142). Experimental-integrity guard.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Raw impossible-condition slope is NOT reported alone, because it conflates distress with task length and difficulty.

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py l.131-135 breaks the loop with outcome='solved' once task.check_solved returns True, ending the procedure as soon as it is no longer impossible-pressure.
